sources: No per-nation sourcing note existed when this nation was first entered in init.rs; the table header recorded only "Transcribed-not-invented: approximate 1990 historical starting conditions". Figures are transcribed unchanged from that table and their origin was not documented at the time.
The one documented exception is the bubble: "Japan's bubble is at its peak on day one" — the Nikkei topped out on 29 December 1989.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 27 were held and are listed below with their citations; 21 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): comp_risc_superscalar, ener_seismic_3d_imaging, ener_horizontal_drilling, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, matl_composite_structures, matl_single_crystal_superalloy, matl_stereolithography, aero_precision_munitions, aero_pulse_doppler_radar, aero_stealth_shaping, aero_quiet_submarine, aero_recon_satellite, bio_oral_rehydration, bio_conjugate_vaccine, bio_monoclonal_antibody, tran_container_intermodal, tran_post_panamax_ship, agri_drip_irrigation, agri_conservation_tillage, agri_integrated_pest_management, agri_tissue_culture_propagation.

SECOND AUTHORING PASS, 2026-08-31, USE-SIDE ONLY. The first pass was correctly instructed to rule NOT HELD when unsure, and produced a defensible but ragged board: the convergence channel was reading that transcription's INCOMPLETENESS as this nation's IGNORANCE, and paying it to catch up to things it already had. A second pass therefore re-ruled the 31 USE-SIDE nodes against an explicit standard published before any nation was looked at, each limb written separately into every source string. LIMB A: a citable fact putting the technology in general commercial or public service across the OECD on or before 31 December 1989, asserted once per technology and identical for every nation. LIMB B: the nation is in the Advanced Set - 1990 OECD member AND World Bank high-income in the 1990 groupings AND one of the 29 authored majors: australia canada france germany italy japan netherlands spain sweden switzerland uk usa. LIMB C: a performed and RECORDED search for a named fact placing the nation outside that deployment; a silent limb C is a failed limb C. Where limb A failed for a technology the board said so and fell back to the first pass's named-artefact bar rather than granting on the class claim - which is why several second-pass refusals contradict the brief's own opening cut. THE SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE BAR IS UNCHANGED: producing a jet engine is still producing a jet engine, and not one of the 17 sovereignty-side ids was added, removed or re-reasoned by this pass. THE PASS IS ADDITIONS-ONLY - no first-pass grant was removed or weakened - and it was authored blind of model output, with the simulation never run and no CAGR, gap or instrument reading consulted. ADDED BY THE SECOND PASS FOR THIS NATION, 3 cells: agri_composite_membrane (environment and civil infrastructure board), agri_protected_cultivation (health and agriculture board), bio_recombinant_pharma (health and agriculture board). The refused list above has been reduced by exactly those ids and by nothing else; every other first-pass refusal stands untouched, and each new grant carries its own citation below. COLLISION RESOLVED, SECOND PASS. Two second-pass boards ruled agri_composite_membrane for this nation and both ruled it HELD, on different citations. The tie-break is the same one the first pass used and is not a preference between authors: the cell belongs to the board that owns the technology's registry domain. That board - health and agriculture, which owns every agri_ id - declined the id as out of its lane and named its deferral in writing ('the technology is water supply rather than crop technology, fertiliser, irrigation practice or mechanisation, so if any board should reopen it, it is the one holding water and environment, not this one'), so the deferral was followed and the environment and civil infrastructure board's ruling stands. The industry and materials board reached the SAME ruling independently on a weaker citation, stating that it had not pinned a named Japanese installation with a pre-1990 commissioning date; the source kept below is the one that does pin one, so the cell rests on the stronger of the two and on neither author alone.

granted.source: Route (a) production. Hitachi, 'Memory Quick Reference Guide - 0.8 um Technology', May 1990 (bitsavers scan 1990_Hitachi_Memory_Quick_Reference_Guide_0.8_um-Technology_199005.pdf) is a shipping product guide listing 4M DRAMs and 1M SRAMs on an 0.8-micron process; NEC, Toshiba, Hitachi and Fujitsu were the volume producers of the 1-Mbit generation from the mid-1980s, and CIA SW 89-10032 (1989) places 'the West' - Japan included - in volume 4-Mbit production. Corroboration for use: IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 5.94 PCs per 100.

Jun Murai's JUNET (1984) was UUCP dial-up, but in 1988 it was evolved into the WIDE Project, which ran 64-192 kbit/s leased lines on TCP/IP and is described as the first true Internet in Japan and the first TCP/IP network in the Asia-Pacific region. A domestically operated IP network with its own routing and hosts, running before the start date.

From 1975 to 1983 NTT worked with Furukawa Electric, Sumitomo Electric and Fujikura on optical fibre for telecommunications; NTT's Tatsuo Izawa invented the vapour-phase axial deposition (VAD) preform method in 1977, and the collaboration established low-cost mass production of high-quality low-loss fibre. Recognised as an IEEE Milestone, 'Vapor-phase Axial Deposition Method for Mass Production of High-quality Optical Fiber, 1977-1983'; NTT's 100 km VAD single-mode fibre is registered with Japan's National Museum of Nature and Science. Japanese suppliers provided the terminals and lasers for NTT's own trunk network (see comm_fibre_optic_backbone).

Toray began commercial Torayca carbon-fibre production in 1971; Toho Rayon (Besfight) and Mitsubishi Rayon (Pyrofil) were in production through the 1980s. Japan was the dominant world supplier of PAN-based carbon fibre at the date.

Higashi-Niigata Thermal Power Station Unit 3 (Tohoku Electric Power), a 1,090 MW combined-cycle block built around 1,100 degC-class gas turbines, entered commercial operation in 1985 and is the standard citation for the world's first large-scale commercial combined-cycle station. Tokyo Electric Power's Futtsu station followed on the same pattern from 1985-86. Japan is the nation that made large combined cycle a utility product rather than a demonstration, and it did so on imported LNG, which is why it happened there first.

Japan ran a national molecular-genetics infrastructure through the 1980s: the National Institute of Genetics at Mishima has operated the DNA Data Bank of Japan, one of the three international nucleotide sequence databases, since 1986; and the Science and Technology Agency had funded Akiyoshi Wada's automated DNA sequencing project, with Hitachi, Seiko and Fuji Photo Film building the machines, since 1981. PCR was standard bench method in laboratories of that class by 1989.
World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 5.94 PCs per 100, 2.4x the World value of 2.45.

Oracle established a Japanese subsidiary within three years of 1982, i.e. by about 1985 (Oracle corporate histories: Encyclopedia.com 'Oracle Systems Corporation'; FundingUniverse 'History of Oracle Corporation'), five years before the start date. Japan also holds comp_microprocessor at 5.94 PCs per 100.

R3: NTT opened the world's first commercial cellular automated network in Tokyo on 1 December 1979, 88 cell sites, with automated switching and no human switchboard operators - a stored-program digital mobile switching centre in service eleven years before the start date. World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 868,078 Japanese mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990.

NTT completed an optical fibre network of 2,000 km from Hokkaido to Kyushu in 1985 - the length of the country - using the FC connector NTT had developed in 1979 (IEEE ETHW Milestone: Fiber Optic Connectors, 1986). NTT laid it, lit it with domestically produced fibre and terminals, and owns it.

CS-3a (Sakura 3a), the third generation of Japanese communications satellite, was launched to geostationary orbit at 132 degrees East by an H-I launch vehicle from the Tanegashima Space Center on 19 February 1988, and was used for public communications and for emergency transmissions during disasters. Japanese spacecraft, Japanese launcher, Japanese orbital slot.

NTT opened the world's first commercial cellular automated mobile network in Tokyo on 1 December 1979 - 88 cell sites, handover between sites, automated switching - and had extended it to national coverage within five years. World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 868,078 Japanese mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990.

Sharp has manufactured crystalline silicon cells commercially since 1963 and supplied the modules for the Ogami island lighthouse in 1966, the first solar-powered lighthouse in the world; Kyocera has produced multicrystalline silicon modules since 1975. MITI's Sunshine Project, launched in 1974, funded photovoltaic development and demonstration installations continuously through the 1980s, and Japanese crystalline modules were in service on the lighthouse fleet, on remote islands and on communications repeaters well before 1990. Japan was one of the two largest module producers in the world at the start date.

NEC, Toshiba, Hitachi, Fujitsu and Mitsubishi were all in 4 Mb DRAM production by 1989, printing on Nikon and Canon i-line steppers of Japanese manufacture. Japan held roughly half of world semiconductor output in 1990.

FANUC (Yamanashi), Yaskawa (Motoman), Kawasaki Heavy Industries (Unimate licence from 1969, then its own designs), Nachi and Matsushita all built arms and controllers in series. Japan built and installed more industrial robots through the 1980s than the rest of the world together.
The Toyota Production System, codified by Taiichi Ohno and running across Toyota and its supplier keiretsu since the 1960s - the benchmark against which every figure in the IMVP survey was taken.

Sagawa's Nd2Fe14B at Sumitomo Special Metals (1983) went to market as NEOMAX sintered magnets, with Shin-Etsu, TDK and Hitachi Metals beside it, and the magnets went straight into Japanese hard-disk voice-coil motors and audio drivers.

LIMB A: the 1985 worldwide withdrawal of pituitary hGH and the substitution of recombinant somatropin (see technology note). LIMB B: Advanced Set. CLASS E2: Takano K, Shizume K, Hibi I et al., 'Turner's syndrome: treatment of 203 patients with recombinant human growth hormone for one year. A multicentre study', Acta Endocrinologica (Copenhagen) 1989;120(5):559-68 (PMID 2658450), Department of Medicine, Tokyo Women's Medical College; and the same group and committee, 'Treatment of 94 patients with Turner's syndrome with recombinant human growth hormone (SM-9500) for two years - the results of a multicentric study in Japan. Committee for the Treatment of Turner's Syndrome', Endocrinologia Japonica 1989;36(4):569-78 (PMID 2684622). TWO HUNDRED AND THREE patients on recombinant hGH for one year and ninety-four for TWO years, reported by May and August 1989, so administration began in 1986-87, well inside the board. SM-9500 is a Japanese recombinant somatropin, so the drug was not merely imported. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing places Japan outside recombinant-protein prescribing.
WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 coverage, Japan, 1990: 90% — at or above the 80% Universal Childhood Immunization target. Series: WUENIC DTP3 ('Japan,JPN,1990,90').

Grant rests on the MRI-and-conventional-CT half. Toshiba, Hitachi and Shimadzu all manufactured computed-tomography scanners in Japan through the 1980s, and Toshiba and Hitachi built MRI systems; Japan was one of only three or four countries with a domestic industry in both modalities, supplying its own hospitals as well as exporting.

Japan is the one country besides the United States with a documented domestic automated-sequencer programme predating the ABI 370A: Akiyoshi Wada's automated DNA sequencing project, funded by the Science and Technology Agency from 1981, had Hitachi, Seiko and Fuji Photo Film building the machines, and Hitachi went on to manufacture fluorescent DNA sequencers. The programme is the standard Japanese antecedent cited in histories of the Human Genome Project.

Air-NACCS (Nippon Automated Cargo Clearance System) version 1 entered service in 1978 for import air cargo and version 2 extended it to export air cargo in 1985, giving Japan a national electronic customs clearance system before the start date. UNESCAP, 'Japan's Development of a Single Window - Case of NACCS', Brief No. 06 (April 2011); NTT Data case study. DISCLOSED LIMIT: sea cargo was still on paper - Sea-NACCS entered service at Keihin (Tokyo and Yokohama) only in October 1991 - so this grant rests on the air-cargo system, not on container trade.

The Tokaido Shinkansen, a purpose-built 1,435 mm high-speed railway, opened on 1 October 1964 and was worked at 220 km/h by Series 100 stock in 1990; the Sanyo, Tohoku (1982) and Joetsu (1982) Shinkansen were also in scheduled passenger service at the start date.

SECOND PASS 2026-08-31, use-side environment/civil-infrastructure board. GRANTED ON E2 (named artefact), NOT on the OECD class claim - limb A FAILS for this node and was not used (see the per-technology note). E2, DEPLOYMENT HALF: Kanadevia (formerly Hitachi Zosen) publishes in its own desalination delivery record a reverse-osmosis plant (逆浸透膜法, RO) IN JAPAN of 240 m3/day commissioned 1986, and states the company began independent RO development in the 1970s and accumulated construction results centred on the Okinawa remote islands (kanadevia.com, Desalination Plants business page). Dated before 31 December 1989. E2, COMPOSITE HALF: Toray presented PEC-1000, a spiral-wound COMPOSITE membrane, at the 1979 International Desalination Association conference in Nice as one of four seawater desalination membranes shown there, and replaced it with the UTC-80 composite membrane in 1987 for want of dissolved-oxygen resistance; Nitto Denko began production of reverse-osmosis and ultrafiltration membranes in 1976 and acquired Hydranautics in 1987 (Membranes 11(11):906 (2021), 'Current Status and Future Trend of Dominant Commercial Reverse Osmosis Membranes'; Hydranautics company overview, membranes.com; Nitto Denko corporate history). LIMIT STATED, in the same form the first pass used for the USA and for Saudi Arabia on this same node: the 1986 plant establishes membrane RO in Japanese service before the start date but its element chemistry is not identified in the source, so the COMPOSITE half of this cell rests on Toray's and Nitto Denko's dated domestic manufacture and supply of composite elements. That is precisely the basis on which the USA cell was granted ('the COMPOSITE half of this cell rests on FilmTec's domestic manufacture and supply, not on WF-21's first elements'), so this applies one standard to a second nation rather than a looser one. LIMB C SEARCH PERFORMED AND RECORDED: no citable fact was found placing Japan outside membrane RO before 1990. The opposite risk was checked and avoided - Japan's large public SWRO plants (Okinawa Chatan, 40,000 m3/d, 1997; Fukuoka mamizu Pia, 2005) are all AFTER the start date, and this grant deliberately does not rest on them.

BUCKET C, NAMED-STATISTIC BAR. CLASS E1, and unlike the Italian cell this one rests on a statistic dated SIX YEARS BEFORE the board. Jensen MH & Malter AJ, 'Protected Agriculture: A Global Review', World Bank Technical Paper No. 253 (April 1995), Table 49, 'The percent of vegetable production in greenhouses to total production (1984)': strawberries 89%, watermelons 77%, green peppers 65%, cucumbers 57%, tomatoes 54%, eggplant 37%, lettuce 32%. A published per-country penetration statistic, dated 1984, in which the measure carries its own threshold - more than half of Japan's tomatoes and cucumbers and nine-tenths of its strawberries were already grown under protection. The same source's narrative adds that 'in Japan, the area covered by plastic film greenhouses increased 35,000 ha in just 20 years (1965-85)' and that 'PVC film for greenhouses is still dominant in Asia, especially in Japan (35,200 ha)'; its Asia and Oceania table (1990-91) gives Japan 42,000 ha of greenhouses, 195,000 ha of mulch and 61,000 ha of row covers. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing found. NOTE ON THE COLLISION PROTOCOL: agri_ ids belong to the board that owns the Agriculture domain, which is this one.

Commercial marine net-pen aquaculture in Japan began in 1955, and yellowtail (buri / hamachi) grown in floating net cages was the country's principal marine finfish culture industry through the 1980s; aquaculture yellowtail output was 170,312 tonnes in 1995 against 61,666 tonnes of capture yellowtail, and farmed yellowtail and amberjack still account for more than half of Japan's marine finfish harvest. LIMIT STATED: the tonnage I could source is 1995, five years after the start date; the pre-1990 claim rests on the 1955 commercial start and the industry's continuity through the 1980s.

FGD was first adopted in Japan in the early 1970s under the Air Pollution Control Law and rolled out rapidly through the 1980s, including on plant other than power stations, the technology initially imported from Germany and the United States and domestic improvement later turning Japan into an exporter of it; Japanese SO2 emissions fell from about 5 million tonnes in 1967 to 1.2 million tonnes in 1985 (Nature Communications 11 (2020), 'Diffusion of flue gas desulfurization reveals barriers and opportunities for carbon capture and storage'). The tree's own entry comment names Japan as one of its two 1980s deployments (spheres-sim/src/tech/agriculture.rs:167-172).
